Both beaches are busy shared environments , with strict rules in place for vehicle users to ensure the safety of beachgoers and vehicle users alike . <p> However , the Auckland Conservation Board says both beaches are also home to particularly fragile dune systems and native biodiversity that need to be protected ; and is asking visitors to please be mindful of this when out enjoying our beautiful beaches . <p> " Auckland is experiencing a great loss of biodiversity , due to the increasing pressures of urban and industrial growth across the @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ due to heavy vehicle usage , high tides and the impact of climate change , " says Ms Mayes . " While significant dune protection work has been undertaken to protect them from erosion , vehicles are still being driven through areas where they are not permitted , and this is also having a major impact on threatened native species which tend to live and nest in , and around , the dune areas . " <p> Ms Mayes says populations of shorebirds that breed and roost in these ecosystems , such as the at-risk northern NZ dotterel , variable oystercatcher and banded dotterel ( threatened ) are vulnerable to disturbance , predation , weather and other natural events . It is important for people to help in any way they can to ease the stress of raising chicks on our beaches over the summer . <p> " It is imperative visitors to the beaches stay away from the dunes -- this means all vehicles , including ATVs and motorbikes . While it might seem fun to drive over the dunes , vehicles can damage plant populations , including native @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ at-risk species ) and spinifex , which can subsequently undermine the structure of the dune systems and put them at risk of further erosion . Driving over dunes is also a safety risk as vehicles can easily roll or become trapped in the sand . <p> Ms Mayes adds that it is important to note that driving vehicles on beaches such as Muriwai poses a threat to seals , which are at risk of being hit by the vehicles -- especially during high tides . <p> " If you have to drive on beaches , do not drive vehicles closer than 50 metres of a marine mammal if you can , and give seals and sea lions space -- stay at least 20 metres away . " <p> " Summer is also an especially busy season for Aotea ( Great Barrier Island ) . We 'd like to remind visitors to the island to avoid driving on estuaries and beaches such as Kaitoke , Awana , Medlands and Whangapoua . " <p> " Ultimately , we wish for all Aucklanders to be able to enjoy our stunning beaches in the @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ to ensure that vehicle access on these beaches is limited to the areas in which they are permitted , and that all users adhere to the rules and guidelines as outlined by the Auckland Council , " says Ms Mayes . <p> " It 's also worth reminding every visitor to our beaches this summer to be mindful of the native species that nest in and around sand dunes ; and help protect them by keeping dogs on a lead and taking their rubbish home with them -- we need to keep our beaches clean so they can continue to be enjoyed by us all . " <p> The Auckland Conservation Board is an independent public advisory body that works in partnership with local communities and iwi to represent local interests in Auckland 's conservation management . 
@@32462056 <p> Year 2020 was the most challenging year any New Zealand government has faced . It was the year of Covid , the year of economic recession and the beginning of recovery . <p> Prime Minister Jacinda Ardern not only led the country through it , but she also won an unprecedented election victory at the end of it . <p> When Ms Ardern held her last post-Cabinet press conference of 2020 , she recalled that when she held the first one she had spoken about the New Zealanders in China 's Hubei Province where a new and deadly virus was reported to have broken out . <p> Horrendous 2020 <p> That covered the entire year , and when she was asked to describe 2020 in two words , she said she could do it in one : " Horrendous . " <p> It was . The first cases of what was to become known as Covid-19 appeared in Wuhan City in December 2019 and began to spread around the world . <p> New Zealand 's first cases were reported in early March and quickly increased . <p> On March @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ 4 lockdown with the words : " Be strong but be kind , we will be okay . " <p> It was set for a month and extended for five days . It worked , and cases decreased . Alert levels were lowered until there were no new community cases being reported . The government had decided on an elimination strategy , it was not going to try to contain the virus and live with it . <p> Bloomfield , Clark <p> Director General of Health Dr Ashley Bloomfield became a household name and a trusted communicator -- T-shirts with his face on them started to appear . <p> He then broke the travel rules by going to a beach with his family , and that was the end of him . <p> Ms Ardern kept him on despite opposition and media pressure , but Clark eventually resigned on 2 July saying " it is the best that I step aside . " <p> It was , and Chris Hipkins took over the health portfolio . <p> Director General of Health Dr Ashley Bloomfield at the back and the then @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ by Dom Thomas ) <p> And Lees-Galloway <p> He was not the only ministerial casualty of the year . Workplace Relations &amp; safety and Immigration Minister Iain Lees-Galloway was dismissed by Ardern on 22 July after it was revealed that he had carried on an affair with a woman who had previously worked in his office and was based in one of his agencies . <p> " His position as a Minister was untenable . The Minister has shown a lack of judgment over a period of 12 months , " Ms Ardern said . <p> These were brief distractions from what was really concerning the nation and the government . <p> The Ministry of Health had set up testing and contact tracing systems which at first were problematic . Border security was vital and managed isolation facilities were set up for people entering the country . There were issues there as well , but they were worked through . <p> Appalling economic impact <p> The economic impact was appalling . The government 's debt reduction targets went out the window as it borrowed $60 billion to cover the cost @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ to avoid lay-offs . <p> It seemed awful , but most of the rest of the world was in far worse shape . <p> The government 's strategy was praised internationally and New Zealand was held up as an example of what could be achieved through strong leadership , honest communication and public support for emergency measures . <p> Ms Ardern put it down to the efforts of her " team of five million . " <p> There were subsequent outbreaks , notably in Auckland , but vigilance won and they were dealt with . <p> The Royal Commission of Inquiry into the killings reported in December concluding there was " no plausible way he the gunman could have been detected except by chance " by state agencies . <p> It put up 44 recommendations on issues ranging from gun law administration to hate speech law , and the government accepted them all . <p> The ' Covid Election ' <p> The election which had been scheduled for 19 September was delayed until October 17 , 2020 because a two-week lockdown in Auckland had restricted campaigning . <p> The Prime @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ Covid Election ' and , as well as campaigning , held frequent pandemic briefings usually carried live by TV networks and media websites . <p> Opposition parties did not like it but could not do anything about it . <p> Ms Ardern never said " trust me to keep you safe " but that was the message and it helped Labour win 65 seats in Parliament . <p> She formed the first majority government since MMP was introduced in 1996 . <p> Disaster for National Party <p> National suffered a dreadful defeat , its caucus reduced from the 56 seats it won in 2017 to 33 , and there is little doubt that the Party 's self-inflicted disasters were a factor in Labour 's unprecedented victory . <p> Simon Bridges was its Leader at the beginning of the year . Despite his low personal popularity ratings , National was strong in the polls and some surveys showed it could win an election . <p> When the pandemic struck and the government began taking strenuous measures to control it , Mr Bridges decided to go on the attack . He criticised @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ were having . He persistently and unfavourably compared those measures with Australia 's less severe restrictions and blamed the government for the vast debt that was being incurred . He had read the public wrong . <p> Todd Muller decided it was time to strike . With popular Auckland MP Nikki Kaye by his side , he forced a caucus leadership vote and on 22 May became the leader of the National Party with Kaye as his Deputy . It was reported , but never confirmed , that the result was very close and there could have been just one vote in it . <p> This was happening in the middle of a pandemic when people were worried about catching a potentially fatal disease and whether their jobs and businesses would survive . <p> Seeing National totally absorbed with itself did not impress them . <p> That was bad but there was worse to come . Muller 's leadership lasted just 53 days and on July 14 , 2020 , he resigned saying : " It has become clear to me that I am not the best person to be @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ . " <p> Mr Muller had not done well . His leadership was beset with problems from the beginning when in a TV interview at his home a red cap carrying US President Donald Trump 's slogan ' Make America Great Again ' was prominent on a shelf in the background . <p> Former Party President Michelle Boag confessed to being the one who sent him the information , gained through her position with the Auckland Rescue Helicopter Trust . She had also sent it to National Party Health Spokesperson Michael Woodhouse but he did not do anything with it . <p> Mr Muller had been under intense media scrutiny since winning the leadership , and it was becoming obvious he was not up to it . <p> His resignation threw National into disarray with the Party looking as though it could not run itself , let alone run a country . The rot had to be stopped , and an emergency Caucus meeting was called on the night of Muller 's resignation . <p> Judith Collins swings <p> The MPs turned to Judith Collins , who had stood for @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ Collins came out swinging , vowing to hold Ardern to account and saying her Party could " crush " the government in the election . <p> Look at my eyebrows-it is a joke-Judith Collins ( Picture for Newsroom by Lynn Grieveson ) <p> The Falloon Scandal <p> Ms Collins then found herself dealing with another scandal . The parents of a young woman aged over 18 notified the prime minister 's office that their daughter had received an indecent image sent by National 's Rangitata MP Andrew Falloon . <p> Ms Ardern 's office forwarded the information to Ms Collins ' office . She dealt with it and Mr Falloon resigned on July 20 , 2020 . <p> Ms Collins scrambled to put a campaign together but time was running out and there was a pitfall ahead . Denise Lee , one of her Auckland MPs , sent an email to the entire Caucus , complaining about Collins ' leadership style . <p> It was leaked to the media , along with disparaging comments from other , unidentified MPs also unhappy about the way Ms Collins was running the show @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ Ardern over the plight of the economy , border security breaches and her government 's failure to meet its child poverty reduction targets . She gave it her best shot but against the backdrop of internal mayhem and damaging leaks she was heading for a hiding . <p> " Disunity is death , " she said after the election , promising that there will not be any more of it and she would show New Zealand " a new National Party . " <p> Ms Collins also said Covid-19 and the government 's focus on it had obscured important issues such as the economic recovery , infrastructure and child poverty . She was right , but it was too late .
